unfold.unfolded: Let $G$ be an almost simple group, and let $G^{\mathrm{reg},\mathrm{uni}}$ be the set of regular unipotent elements of $G$. Then $$G^{\mathrm{reg},\mathrm{uni}}\cap G_{\geqslant 0}=\bigsqcup_{w\in W,\ \operatorname{supp}(w)=I}U^+_{w,>0}\ \sqcup\ \bigsqcup_{w\in W,\ \operatorname{supp}(w)=I}U^-_{w,>0}.$$ In particular, $G^{\mathrm{reg},\mathrm{uni}}\cap G_{\geqslant 0}$ has two connected components, and they are dense in the unipotent radicals of two opposite Borel subgroups $B^+$ and $B^-$ of $G$.
assumed: support of an element of the Weyl group
notes: The notation G_{≥0}, U^±_{w,>0}, I and B^± is not defined in the context, so it is kept as the paper writes it.
I read W as the Weyl group of G and I as the index set of its simple roots, as usual.
